entries.result: On printed p9 the 1935 report explicitly describes a July24 message sent by LP (Berlin) to COS (Tiflis) through NKJ (Nicolaiev), then prints NKJ v LP and FUER COS. entries.claim_reviewed: The context-supplied digit 6 securely identifies the German 6th Reserve Division in the Balkans in November 1918.
entries.result: The cited French telegram really prints a 6th reserve infantry division while reporting the situation on November 11. However the U.S. War Department divisional history places the German 6th Reserve Division in France in 1918 and says it was dissolved shortly after its relief in early August. The French report is therefore contextual support for the published wording, not a fully reconciled unit identification. No alternative digit or unit is assigned here, and the three unassigned square cells remain unassigned.

entries.claim_reviewed: The original 6th Reserve Division’s August 1918 dissolution makes a November 6.R.D. reference in the Balkans historically impossible.

attribution.author: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro source review

entries.result: The original infantry formation was dissolved, but that does not exclude continued employment of its headquarters. Ruhmeshalle unserer alten Armee, 5th edition, volume 1, p385 explicitly places 6.R.-D. in the Macedonia/Serbia retreat and lists its November return through Hungary. Cron’s organizational history separately says the dissolved division’s staff was to be used in Macedonia. The French 6e D.I. réserve wording is therefore contextually plausible; no unknown cipher cell or missing digit is assigned.

entries.result: The original page explicitly dates the two CHI parts to November 8 and labels them parts 5 and 6, with lengths 132 and 108. Part 6 preserves exactly 15 printed dashes after the first five-coordinate group. Its first group is clearly AXVAA: any change to the final two A coordinates is an explicit emendation, not a source-transcription correction. A bounded search of the archived 2017 challenge comments, current Bourdeau/baseline material, the complete book OCR, the independently decrypted source index, and NSA report texts found no earlier reading matching the newly recovered phrases. Public web searches combining ADFGVX with ANORDNUNGEN and MUNITIONSBESTAND also found no matching solution. This search does not prove unrestricted worldwide novelty.

verification_evidence.primary_source: J. Rives Childs collection, printed p. 153 / Aegean PDF p. 156
verification_evidence.historical_distinction_source: German Military Ciphers from February to November 1918 (1935), printed p. 14 / PDF p. 22
verification_evidence.historical_distinction: Childs distinguishes western CHI messages with daily key changes from eastern RICHI messages with multi-day key periods. The p153 order therefore cannot be assigned to the Balkan 11th Army merely from its position in a RICHI-labelled source log. FKR and CGH remain unidentified station calls.
verification_evidence.limit: This entry records archival and prior-art checks; the independent cipher certificate supplies the mathematical verification and its explicit uncertainty domains.

entries.claim_reviewed: The shared unknown key for the two November 8 CHI fragments yields a substantial new partial reading.

Each partial key still admits 17! square completions; this is not a claim of global historical uniqueness.

conditional_width_screen.independent_check_limit: Separate exact implementations reproduce the width18 result. entries.claim_reviewed: The Nov7–9 square implies a transposition-invariant rare-letter/digit constraint for p73.
entries.result: The 26 received F coordinates require at least 13 positions from CJMOQZ or digits, or 26 CJMOQZ positions if digit-free. Two held-out books make the target an empirical outlier under joined and sentence-X conventions while the historical control lies inside their reference range. The failed word-X convention is disclosed. No p-value or key exclusion is claimed. The complementary V budget gives n_D+n_E+n_H+n_K+n_Q+n_T+n_U+2n_X <= 17, hence at most eight X characters; with five Xs, at most seven DEHKQTU characters combined.

entries.claim_reviewed: Exact fixed-complete-key dynamic programming covers every five-scattered-loss mask.
entries.result: Four completed cases cover C(170, 5) = 1,115,034,284 masks each via 15,504 column allocations. The optimum is for the quantized mean-domain quad table. One true-key control prefers a wrong geometry; historical fixed-completion optima remain unreadable.

entries.claim_reviewed: The joint optimizer chooses missing positions and six-valued fills consistently across all overlapping windows.

Four full runs, 10,188 exhaustive small witnesses, canonical ties and every retained source coordinate were checked independently.

entries.claim_reviewed: An exact count objective bounds all 40,320 completions of the Nov13–15b partial square under its fixed transposition and every five-loss/fill witness.

entries.claim_reviewed: Exact six-gram and mixed joint decoding recover one planted true-key control and retain a counterexample for the other.
entries.result: Two full CHI13 searches cover all 8,670,506,592,384 loss-and-fill witnesses and recover the planted 85-letter text, five loss positions and their values. Both objectives still score a feasible wrong Nov13b text above truth. The four- and six-gram tables share a corpus; separate held-out-book diagnostics preserve the second failure.
